name: APIs & Microservices
description: Designing HTTP APIs, REST, GraphQL and gRPC, and building, connecting and operating microservices.

nodes.name: HTTP for APIs
nodes.desc: Methods, status codes, headers, caching and idempotency from an API designer's view.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use HTTP methods, status codes, headers and caching deliberately when designing an API, including idempotency guarantees.

nodes.name: API styles
nodes.desc: REST, RPC, GraphQL and event-based APIs compared.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare REST, RPC, GraphQL and event-based APIs and choose the style that fits a given use case.

nodes.name: Data formats
nodes.desc: JSON, schemas, Protocol Buffers and serialisation trade-offs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose between JSON and Protocol Buffers, define schemas and weigh serialisation trade-offs for API payloads.
topics: Protocol Buffers messages and field numbers
Size and speed of text versus binary

nodes.name: REST design
nodes.desc: Resources, URIs, verbs, status codes and consistent error responses.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design consistent REST APIs with sensible resource URIs, correct verbs and status codes and uniform error responses.
topics: Status codes for success and failure

nodes.name: Paging & versioning
nodes.desc: Pagination, filtering, sorting and evolving an API without breaking clients.
nodes.summary: You will be able to add pagination, filtering and sorting to collections and evolve an API without breaking existing clients.
topics: URI, header and media type versioning

nodes.name: OpenAPI
nodes.desc: Describing APIs with OpenAPI and generating docs and clients.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe an HTTP API in an OpenAPI document and generate documentation, clients and validation from it.

nodes.name: API auth
nodes.desc: API keys, OAuth 2.0, JWTs and scopes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to secure APIs with API keys, OAuth 2.0 flows and JWT access tokens limited by scopes.

nodes.name: GraphQL
nodes.desc: Schemas, queries, mutations, resolvers and the N+1 problem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define a GraphQL schema, write queries and mutations, implement resolvers and avoid the N+1 query problem.
topics: The N+1 problem and DataLoader batching

nodes.name: gRPC
nodes.desc: Protobuf services, streaming RPCs and when gRPC fits.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define gRPC services in Protobuf, use unary and streaming RPCs and judge when gRPC is a good fit.
topics: Unary, server, client and bidirectional streaming
gRPC versus REST for internal services

nodes.name: Webhooks & WebSockets
nodes.desc: Push-based APIs with webhooks, WebSockets and server-sent events.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build push-based APIs with webhooks, WebSockets and server-sent events and choose between them.

nodes.name: Microservices
nodes.desc: What microservices are, their benefits and costs versus a monolith.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain what microservices are and weigh their benefits and operational costs against a well-structured monolith.

nodes.name: Service boundaries
nodes.desc: Domain-driven design, bounded contexts and splitting a monolith.
nodes.summary: You will be able to draw service boundaries using domain-driven design and plan an incremental split of a monolith.

nodes.name: Service communication
nodes.desc: Synchronous calls versus asynchronous messaging and events.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose between synchronous calls and asynchronous messaging between services and understand the coupling each creates.

nodes.name: Gateways & discovery
nodes.desc: API gateways, service discovery and service meshes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how API gateways, service discovery and service meshes route and secure traffic between clients and services.

nodes.name: Data per service
nodes.desc: Database per service, sagas and eventual consistency between services.
nodes.summary: You will be able to keep data consistent across services that own separate databases using sagas and eventual consistency.

nodes.name: Resilience
nodes.desc: Timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers and bulkheads.
nodes.summary: You will be able to protect services from cascading failures with timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers and bulkheads.
topics: Retries with exponential backoff and jitter

nodes.name: Tracing & metrics
nodes.desc: Distributed tracing, correlation IDs, metrics and structured logs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to observe a distributed system using traces, correlation IDs, metrics and structured logs.

nodes.name: Contract testing
nodes.desc: Consumer-driven contracts and testing services in isolation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test services in isolation and catch breaking API changes early with consumer-driven contract tests.

nodes.name: Public API project
nodes.desc: Build and document a versioned, authenticated public REST API.
nodes.summary: You will build and document a versioned, authenticated public REST API with pagination, consistent errors and an OpenAPI specification.
topics: Authentication with API keys or OAuth

nodes.name: Microservice shop
nodes.desc: Build a small shop as several containerised services with messaging and tracing.
nodes.summary: You will build a small online shop as several containerised services that communicate through messaging and are observable with tracing.
